text:
maria: Heads-up — since ~09:40 UTC a subset of eu-west GPU nodes are failing image pulls for the ml-inference pods. Seemed to start right after the DNS change rolled to edge proxies.

koji: seeing ImagePullBackOff on ~12 nodes, logs show kubernetes trying to resolve registry.internal.prod then falling back to external IP.

sre_jun: Can you paste the pod describe + node resolv.conf? Suspect split-horizon/ndots interaction.

maria: sure — pod describe shows:
```
Events:
  Normal  Pulling    2s (x3 over 1m)  kubelet, gpu-node-17  Pulling image "registry.internal.prod/org/model:latest"
  Warning Failed     1s (x3 over 1m)  kubelet, gpu-node-17  Failed to pull image: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = Get "https://registry.internal.prod/v2/": dial tcp: lookup registry.internal.prod: no such host
```
node /etc/resolv.conf (on gpu-node-17):
```
search eu-west.prod.svc.cluster.local prod.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local
nameserver 10.0.0.10  # node-local-dns
options ndots:5 timeout:2
```

devops_jay: interesting — node-local-dns (10.0.0.10) is returning an external A record for registry.internal.prod in some cases (we patched the edge split-horizon yesterday). The external IP is in the blocked egress range for GPUs (NAT gateway policy).

oncall-bot: incident created: DNS-EGRESS-2066 · severity:low · assigned: @sre_jun

tim: I can repro locally — if the search list gets appended, queries without FQDN get attempted with the long search suffix, and coredns rules for internal zones might not match. I suspect some nodes are issuing queries that hit the global resolver rather than the internal forwarder due to recent resolvconf reorder.

koji: also seeing TTL caching weirdness — node-local-dns cache still has old mapping (internal name -> external IP) with TTL 3600. Even after we updated the split-horizon records the old mapping persisted until cache expired.

sre_jun: quick mitigation steps: 1) restart node-local-dns daemonset on affected nodes (flush cache), 2) add hosts file entry on gpu nodes for registry.internal.prod -> internal VIP, 3) temporarily open egress to the external IP for image pulls while we fix split-horizon. Thoughts?

maria: hosts edit worked for 2 nodes — image pulled after hosts entry. But hosts edits aren’t scalable.

devops_jay: opening egress to external IP is risky (policy + cost) and could mask real split-horizon bug. Prefer flushing the local caches + fix zone config on edge proxies.

tim: command to flush node-local-dns cache quickly:
```
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart daemonset/node-local-dns
kubectl -n kube-system exec -it ds/node-local-dns -- /bin/sh -c "kill -HUP 1"
```

maria: rolled node-local-dns on 5 nodes, those succeeded. But 7 nodes still failing — their resolv.conf shows nameserver order reversed (10.0.0.11 then 10.0.0.10). Looks like DHCP/bootscripts on some GPU hosts applied a different resolvconf update.

koji: that explains inconsistent behavior. The nodes hitting 10.0.0.11 (edge forwarder) get external A; nodes hitting 10.0.0.10 (node-local) get internal VIP. Need to align resolvconf generation.

sre_jun: plan: (A) push fix to edge split-horizon to ensure internal zones are authoritative, (B) force resolvconf template uniformity via chef on gpu host fleet, (C) add a kubelet flag to always use node-local-dns first (ndots tweak?) — rolling out as patch.

devops_jay: note on cost/regional impact — if we failover imagepulls to eu-central registry mirror the egress cost would spike because cross-region bandwidth for large model layers is significant. Dedicated GPU reserved capacity in eu-west would be underutilized if we shift region. We should prefer local fixes.

maria: can we reduce ndots to 1 for kubelet pods? That might avoid search appending for short names and reduce accidental external resolution. But changing ndots cluster-wide has unknown side effects.

konstantin: (infra-bot) FYI: we have a runbook for split-horizon + imagepull issues: https://intranet.redwood/ops/runbooks/dns-splithorizon-imagepull — follow sections "flush caches" and "hosts as temporary workaround".

tim: also noticed some older containerd versions retry differently and surface the error as no such host even when DNS eventually resolves — that makes the window for success small. We should increase image pull timeout on kubelet as stopgap.

sre_jun: action items —
- devops_jay: roll the split-horizon zone patch to edge proxies (priority)
- maria: continue rolling node-local-dns restart across remaining nodes and gather list of nodes with reversed resolv.conf
- koji: prepare chef change for resolvconf template and a flag to pin node-local-dns first
- tim: open PR to bump kubelet imagePull timeout / backoff

maria: +1 on action items. I'll also patch hosts via salt on the remaining 7 as emergency until node-local-dns restarts finish.

devops_jay: started edge proxy patch — rolling 30% now. Monitoring registry queries.

oncall-bot: update: incident DNS-EGRESS-2066 moved to investigating -> mitigated (partial).

maria: most nodes are green after fixes and cache restarts. Reopen if you still see failures. Thanks all :thumbsup:
